html:
Shibam is a walled town in the Hadhramaut valley of eastern Yemen, packed with some 500 tower houses of mud brick, many five to eleven storeys high. Most of today's houses date from the 1500s onward.

The town has been a trading and market centre on the caravan road for much longer. It was built tall inside a tight wall to protect against raids and floods. Its look has earned it the name "Manhattan of the desert", and it is one of the oldest examples of planning by vertical building.

Shibam became a World Heritage Site in 1982. Its houses must be replastered with mud regularly, and floods, neglect and the war have put it at risk. Money sent home by the Hadhrami diaspora long helped maintain such towns in Hadhramaut. Compare Sana'a.
